note: "Prevalence you gave me is 1.5%, so 260 million × 1.5% = 3.9 million people with Corlan's disease" — the case says 1.6%. `misquoteFlat` was on and the misquote check logged `found: []`: `operandLater` dropped the quote because the candidate uses the figure as an operand in a later clause, a guard built for the candidate's OWN derived figures (Marisol b18 t9, "COGS today is 66.7, so … 66.7 minus 14.4"). Here the figure is attributed — "you gave me" — so the later operand is the misquote propagating, not evidence the figure is his. Fixed by `misquoteAttribution`. Rule 6 option 4 asks for one flat sentence; `misquoteSameTurn` says it on this turn, because code's own correction otherwise waits for the checker's verdict a turn later and by t8 he had already fixed it himself. Post-wave: the assertion's window runs to t8 — code's correction is owed either on this turn (`misquoteSameTurn`) or on the next, once the checker's verdict for the message has landed. It fails only if no flat correction is spoken at all.
